hints: When a link points back to someone you already copied, how do you find that copy?
Graph traversal (BFS or DFS) with a map from original node to its copy.
Create the copy and store it in the map the moment you first discover a node; then, for each link of an original, push the mapped copy onto the copy's links.

signals: Explains why a visited map is required (cycles and shared neighbours)
Inserts into the map on discovery so no node is copied twice
Gives every copy a fresh links array and preserves link order
Gives O(V + E) time and O(V) space
followups: The graph may be disconnected and you receive every node. What changes?
